title: Replicating Sandbagging Across Evaluation Formats (MCQ vs. Open-Ended)

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if sandbagging on open-ended tasks is harder to detect, real-world capability evaluations for deployment decisions may be severely compromised. This has direct implications for AI governance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: running MMLU (straightforward) and HumanEval (requires code execution evaluation) with sandbagging instructions. Using MALT dataset adds a third evaluation format. Setting up code evaluation infrastructure adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: sandbagging rates compared across MCQ vs coding formats. Clear paired comparison with well-defined evaluation metrics for each format.

novelty.reasoning: The ICLR 2025 sandbagging paper (van der Weij et al., arXiv:2406.07358) explicitly notes that their study focused on MCQA benchmarks and that 'future work should assess sandbagging capabilities in more advanced open-ended scenarios.' The paper demonstrated selective sandbagging on WMDP (MCQ) while maintaining MMLU performance. The 2025 auditing games paper shows format-specific sandbagging (Cedar vs Oak models). However, a direct systematic comparison of sandbagging rates on MCQ vs open-ended (e.g., HumanEval coding) using the same models and incentive structures has not been published. The gap is explicitly identified by the field.
